reconcile.connective: Clarke revives the old son-in-law theory: Joseph was Jacob's true son in Matthew but Heli's son-in-law in Luke's record of Mary's line.

discrepancy.connective: Bart Ehrman rejects that harmonizing move, noting Luke explicitly calls the line Joseph's, not Mary's, so the two fathers cannot both be right.

skeptic.name: Bart D. Ehrman
skeptic.work: Jesus, Interrupted: Revealing the Hidden Contradictions in the Bible (and Why We Don't Know About Them)

excerpts.excerpt_text: This remark alone is sufficient to remove every difficulty. Thus it appears that Joseph, son of Jacob, according to St. Matthew, was son-in-law of Heli, according to St. Luke.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly answers the Matthew-Jacob vs. Luke-Heli father discrepancy by making Joseph Jacob's actual son (Matthew) and Heli's son-in-law through Mary (Luke) — the single strongest, most concise statement of the son-in-law harmonization theory among the gathered notes.

pd_work.resource: John W. Haley, An Examination of the Alleged Discrepancies of the Bible (1874), pp. 325-326
pd_work.author: John W. Haley
pd_work.note: Haley treats this exact passage under 'Christ's genealogy,' laying out both the Matthew-Joseph/Luke-Joseph theory and the Matthew-Joseph/Luke-Mary theory and preferring the latter: Joseph 'was the actual son of Jacob, and the legal son of Heli' by marrying Heli's heiress daughter Mary.

link.title: GotQuestions: Why are Jesus' genealogies in Matthew and Luke so different?
link.note: Live apologetic page arguing Matthew records Joseph's line and Luke records Mary's, with Joseph called 'son of Heli' by marriage since Koine Greek had no word for son-in-law.
